description: Search a global professional database for people and get a sample of matches plus the true total match count. Ask with `filters` (recommended: state each part exactly, for example {"job_titles": ["M&A Associate", "Investment Banking Associate"], "locations": ["Frankfurt", "Munich"], "industries": ["Investment Banking"], "schools": ["University of Mannheim"]}) or with `query`, a plain-English sentence that is parsed for you (for example 'Heads of Marketing at Series B SaaS in New York'). Results are masked previews (a masked name, role, industry, company size and location) and each one carries an opaque `token`. Searching is FREE and spends no credits: use it to check that the right people come back before you pay, and refine the filters if they do not. If nothing matches exactly, the least essential filters are dropped automatically and `broadenedBy` names them; `ignored` lists any filter that could not be applied. To get a person's real name, LinkedIn and verified email, pass their token to reveal_profile, or use find_people with the same filters to unlock a batch in one call.

filters.description: Exact filters, recommended for AI agents and programs: state each part of the request instead of a sentence. Values inside one list are alternatives (OR); different fields must all match (AND). Give a few variants where people word things differently (titles: ["M&A Associate", "Investment Banking Associate"]). When filters are given, `query` is only a label and is not parsed.

company_domains.description: Current employers by website domain, the most exact way to name a company, e.g. ["stripe.com"].

company_size_max.description: Maximum employees at the current employer.

company_size_min.description: Minimum employees at the current employer.

industries.description: Industry of the current employer, as LinkedIn names it, e.g. ["Investment Banking"], ["Software Development"], ["Hospitals and Health Care"], ["Venture Capital and Private Equity Principals"], ["Staffing and Recruiting"]. Common older names are mapped; a name that is not an industry is reported in `ignored` and not applied.

job_titles.description: Current job titles, matched as case-insensitive substrings ("Account Executive" also finds "Senior Account Executive"). Include the variants people use: ["VP Sales", "Vice President of Sales", "Head of Sales"].

keywords.description: Words to find anywhere on the profile (headline, descriptions, past roles), for what no other field covers.

languages.description: Languages the person speaks, e.g. ["German"] or ["DE"].

locations.description: Where the person lives or works: cities, states, countries or regions, e.g. ["Frankfurt", "Munich"], ["Germany"], ["DACH"], ["Texas"]. Use "City, Country" to tell same-named places apart ("Paris, France"). Country names are safest; ISO codes are converted.

past_companies.description: Former employers by name, e.g. ["McKinsey"] for ex-McKinsey people.

past_job_titles.description: Titles the person held before their current job.

schools.description: Schools the person attended, matched as substrings; add the local-language name too, e.g. ["University of Mannheim", "Universität Mannheim"].

skills.description: Skills listed on the profile, e.g. ["Python", "Kubernetes"].

years_experience_max.description: Maximum total years of professional experience.

years_experience_min.description: Minimum total years of professional experience.

limit.description: How many masked previews to return (1-25, default 10). This does not limit the reported total.

query.description: Who you are looking for, in plain English (role, seniority, industry, company, company size, location). Parsed for you. Optional when `filters` is given, where it is only a label.

name: people_search
title: Search people
